ruling.recommended_action: Send file to a human reviewer: confirm from the dispatched route/GPS breadcrumb whether the 22:54–23:03 off-route segment was actually driven on Guillemard Road; if it was not (or cannot be confirmed), refund $3.01 (2.13 km × $1.4102/km) as a Ryde voucher and flag the driver's account under RD-6.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider-filed route deviation on a metered RydeTAXI trip (NEX Serangoon → Suntec City, 22:41–23:10, $32.28 [F7]). The trace settles ✓ that one off-route segment exists: F3, 22:54–23:03, 3.77 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, +2.13 km extra, up to 1095 m off the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. The trace settles ✗ that no RD-4(a) incident exempts it: F15 records no incident near the route in the trip window, and F12's PIE band 2 (10–19 km/h, 22:32–22:54) is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment alone [F15][F12][RD-4]. The driver's congestion excuse therefore does not excuse the segment [RD-4].

The remaining question is the RD-5 scope of the rider's consent, and the record does not settle it. At 22:51 the driver named a specific road — "mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?" — and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead." [F8][F9]. That message precedes the segment start of 22:54, so the "before" test is met [F9][F3][RD-5]. But a named-road consent reaches only driving on that road, and the record must tie the segment to it: F3 carries no road name for the driven path, and the only placement the record offers is the driver's own post-trip statement, which is a statement, not rider consent [F11][RD-5][G11]. Nothing ties the 22:54–23:03 segment to Guillemard Road, and nothing places it elsewhere. Under G13 that leaves the finding undetermined, not exempt and not counting [F3][F8][F9][RD-5][G13]. RD-3(a) cannot help either way: the trace shows no measured stop and the rider named no specific place [F3][RD-3].

Because this undetermined finding changes both the amount and the account flag, the case goes to a person [RD-5][G12]. If the reviewer confirms the segment was not on Guillemard Road, the refund is 2.13 km × the trip's rate, $19.15 ÷ 13.58 km = $1.4102/km, giving $3.0037 → $3.01 [F3][F7][RD-2]; the residual 0.46 km between the billed 2.59 km and the segment 2.13 km is corridor/map-match residual and is not refunded [F4][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting item is meter waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip and is chargeable, not refundable [F5][RD-3(c)], and any refund issues as a Ryde voucher within the 30-day window [F4][NS-7]. If the segment is confirmed on Guillemard Road it is exempt under RD-5 and no refund follows. If the segment were upheld, the driver's 2 upheld route disputes in 90 d would make it repeated and require the RD-6 account flag [F18][RD-6]; the profile never establishes the detour itself [F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message was 'Sure, go ahead.' at 22:51, answering the driver's request 'mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?' [F8][F9]. A named-road consent under RD-5 covers driving on that road only and the record must tie the segment to it; F3 records no road name for the driven path, and the driver's own post-trip statement is not rider consent [F11][RD-5][G11]. Nothing ties the 22:54–23:03 segment to Guillemard Road and nothing places it elsewhere, so the scope of the consent is undetermined (G13) rather than consented [F3][F8][F9][RD-5][G13]. RD-4 gives no exemption (no incident on the replaced stretch; PIE band 2 is corroboration only) [F15][F12][RD-4], and RD-3(a) does not apply (no measured stop, no rider-named place) [F3][RD-3].

rejected_claims.reason: F3 alone does not establish that the segment is unexempted: the rider's 22:51 message 'Sure, go ahead.' [F9] answers a pre-segment named-road request [F8], so the RD-5 scope must be read before the segment can be charged, and on this record it is undetermined [F3][F8][F9][RD-5][G13].

The refundable head is the unexempted segment's extra_km, not the billed 2.59 km / $3.65 head, and 2.13 km × $1.4102/km = $3.0037 [F3][F4][RD-2]; with the segment undetermined no amount can be executed now [RD-5][G12].
Correct that the record lacks a fact tying the driven segment to Guillemard Road, but that makes the scope undetermined, not a settled ground for refunding the segment [F3][F8][F9][RD-5][G13].
Correct as to F11 (a post-trip driver statement is not consent), but it does not resolve scope: F9 alone meets the timing test without tying the segment to the named road [F11][F9][RD-5][G13].
The RD-6 profile point (F18: 2 route disputes upheld in 90 d) depends on a non-exempt segment being found in this case; the segment is undetermined, so no account flag is executed here [F18][RD-6].
Timing alone satisfies the RD-5 'before' test but proves nothing about scope; no fact ties the driven segment to Guillemard Road [F8][F9][F3][RD-5][G13].

Accepted that no RD-4(a) incident exempts the segment [F15][RD-4], but RD-2 treatment cannot be applied while the RD-5 scope is undetermined, so the case goes to a human rather than to an automatic refund [F3][RD-5][G12].
